canonical_summary: Three Fed regional presidents publicly urged further rate hikes rather than cuts, the first three-way hawkish dissent since 2016, with new Fed Chair Warsh also striking a hawkish tone.
Eurozone flash HICP inflation accelerated to 2.9% y/y in July (core 2.5%), driven by rising energy prices, raising the odds of further ECB tightening at the September meeting.
The S&P 500 closed above 7,700 and the Dow topped 54,000 for the first time as markets rallied on progress toward a US-Iran deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to shipping.
AMD shares fell sharply post-earnings despite a revenue beat, signaling a market shift from AI-buildout growth narrative toward scrutiny of AI capex discipline and returns.
Deutsche Telekom's board raised its 2026 share buyback by up to 3 billion euros, to as much as 5 billion euros total, explicitly to address a depressed share price.

The Czech National Bank unanimously held its base rate at 3.75% but flagged that persistent core inflation and a tight labor market make at least one more hike likely before year-end, while cutting its 2026 growth forecast to 2.2%.
Czech flat prices rose 2.7% q/q in Q1 2026, reaccelerating despite high mortgage rates, with new-build prices in Prague 7 and Prague 8 up as much as 25% y/y.

Industry estimates point to 750 billion to 1 trillion euros of Western European commercial real estate refinancing due by 2030, with Germany alone facing roughly 260 billion euros in maturities, compounded by mandatory energy-efficiency upgrade deadlines through 2033.

The US Senate confirmed it will not vote on the CLARITY Act crypto market-structure bill before its August recess, pushing the effort to define SEC/CFTC jurisdiction over digital assets to mid-September at the earliest.

Putin signed Russia's first comprehensive crypto law, establishing central-bank-licensed exchanges, a retail investment cap, and legalized crypto-based cross-border trade settlement starting September, while keeping domestic crypto payments banned.
US spot Bitcoin ETFs logged 626 million dollars in net inflows over the first three trading days of August, ending a run that included July's worst monthly outflows of 2026.
US copper hit a record price as a 50% US tariff on semi-finished copper products drove import hoarding just as mine supply was constrained in Indonesia and hit by storms in Chile.
Central banks bought a record 289 tonnes of gold in Q2 2026, up 62% y/y and led by Poland, with gold now exceeding US Treasuries as a share of global official reserves.
X-Energy and Centrus signed a long-term enriched nuclear fuel supply agreement for small modular reactors, part of a wave of nuclear-fuel deals driven by surging AI data-center power demand.

Datadog shares fell nearly 20%, their largest single-day drop on record, despite beating Q2 estimates and raising full-year guidance, as investors fixated on one large AI customer signaling reduced usage for H2.
The US and Japan conducted their first joint yen-buying intervention since 1998 after the yen hit a roughly four-decade low near 163/USD; gains had partly reversed by August 7.
Palantir shares jumped ~29% after Q2 2026 revenue grew 93% YoY and the company sharply raised full-year guidance on strong US commercial demand.
Caterpillar posted its first-ever 0B+ quarter and a record backlog (+92% YoY to 2B), driven substantially by AI-datacenter power-generation demand.
Camden Property Trust sold its entire California apartment portfolio (11 properties, .63B) to BlackRock, the largest US multifamily transaction since 2024.
A 2021 firmware bug in Coinkite Coldcard hardware wallets enabled attackers to brute-force keys, draining over 00 million in Bitcoin since late July 2026.
Tether's Hadron platform will launch institutional real-estate tokenization in Saudi Arabia with First Advanced Data for AI and BKN301, under Vision 2030.
The DRC banned exports of copper and cobalt concentrates effective August 6, 2026 to force domestic processing, adding a fresh supply shock to both metals.
KKR closed its largest-ever infrastructure fund at 9.2B and agreed to buy a 50% stake in a European renewables portfolio from TotalEnergies.
AppLovin shares fell ~19-21% after missing the midpoint of its own revenue guidance for the first time since IPO; analysts split on whether it is a buying opportunity.
US July nonfarm payrolls unexpectedly fell 23,000 with wage growth slowing to 3.2% y/y, sharply cutting September Fed rate-hike odds from ~55-58% to ~40-44% just a day after hawkish Fed commentary.
Banco de México held its overnight rate at 6.50% for a second straight meeting, pausing after 475bp of cumulative cuts since early 2024 to assess prior easing.

Oklo's Groves reactor achieved first criticality roughly 11 months after groundbreaking, the first DOE Reactor Pilot Program project to go from greenfield to critical, sending shares up over 10% despite an EPS miss.
Vistra reported Q2 GAAP net income of $305M and adjusted EBITDA of $1.77B (up from $1.35B y/y) as merchant power generators keep benefiting from AI data-center electricity demand.
The Russell 2000 crossed 3,000 for the first time, with small caps up ~20.7% YTD versus the S&P 500's ~12.8%, extending a broadening market-leadership rotation.
Freddie Mac's 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose to 6.69%, a fifth straight weekly increase and the highest level of 2026, continuing to squeeze US housing affordability.

UWM Holdings posted a $451.9M Q2 net loss, suspended its dividend for the first time, and took a $2.05B dilutive preferred equity/warrant investment from Oaktree and the Ishbia family, with shares down 35-49%.
Zillow cut 500 jobs (its second 2026 round) and reported Q2 revenue of $772M (+18% y/y) but gave soft forward guidance, sending shares down ~6% after hours.

NYC's DOB concluded a safety sweep of 180 office-to-residential conversion sites triggered by a July structural failure, finding violations at 38 sites but ruling the failure was not systemic to the conversion method.
Commercial real estate lending REITs Sunrise Realty Trust and Southern Realty Trust announced a definitive stock merger, part of a wider 2026 wave of CRE lending REIT consolidation.
Data-center REITs continued outperforming the broader REIT index, with UK-listed Tritax Big Box announcing a ~£350M capital raise for London data-center projects backed by 235MW of secured power.

A draft Ethereum proposal (EIP-8363) to progressively burn validator staking rewards as staking ratio rises drew public opposition from Aave's founder, ether.fi's CEO, and corporate ETH treasury holder SharpLink Gaming.

Circle renewed its USDC distribution agreement with Coinbase through 2029, resolving prior friction, while confirming it will not pay dividends and will reinvest toward AI-agent payment infrastructure instead.

Boerse Stuttgart's crypto arm completed its merger with institutional trading firm Tradias, forming a ~300-employee European regulated digital-asset infrastructure provider serving major banks under MiCA.

Iran and Oman reached a framework agreement on a phased Strait of Hormuz shipping corridor, but Iran then added fresh conditions (banning 'hostile' vessels, fines) before full reopening, pushing oil prices back up.
The copper squeeze widened from COMEX to the LME as US and Chinese buyers competed for physical metal, setting fresh records before a sharp profit-taking reversal by August 8.

Gold, silver, and platinum all rallied to multi-month highs on Fed rate-cut bets after the weak jobs report, with major gold ETF inflows of over $600M in a single day and platinum breaking above $1,700.
Energy Capital Partners closed its largest-ever infrastructure fund at $8.1B, over 80% larger than its predecessor, deploying into nuclear services, LNG, and multi-energy distribution.

The Trade Desk fell ~27-28% to a 7-year low after guiding to its first-ever revenue decline, splitting analysts sharply between deep target cuts and reiterated buy ratings citing an oversold valuation.

Sandisk fell ~10-13% despite a blowout quarter with data-center revenue more than doubling sequentially, purely on guidance modestly below consensus, which analysts called a disproportionate reaction.
Sezzle fell ~22% despite record Q2 revenue growth of ~52% y/y, after guiding H2 growth to moderate to ~30% and flagging normalizing transaction yields.

China's July 2026 CPI rose just 0.5% year-on-year, below the 0.8% forecast and the slowest pace since January, while PPI slowed to 3.5% from 4.1%, deepening deflation concerns despite strong export growth.

Berkshire Hathaway reported Q2 2026 net earnings more than doubling to $25.7 billion, resumed aggressive share buybacks ($4.5B, up from $235M in Q1), and became a net buyer of equities for the first time in 15 quarters, including a $10 billion addition to its Alphabet stake, as CEO Greg Abel began deploying the company's record cash hoard.

Atlassian shares surged roughly 30-36% after fiscal Q4 2026 results showed cloud revenue growth accelerating to 31% year over year, a return to GAAP operating profitability, and forward guidance above consensus.

Twilio shares jumped roughly 17-28% after Q2 2026 results beat estimates and the company sharply raised full-year revenue growth guidance to 18-18.5% from a prior 14-15%, citing accelerating demand for its cloud communications and voice AI products.

SpaceX's first post-IPO insider lockup expired on August 6, freeing roughly $123 billion worth of shares (about 911.5 million shares) for potential sale and more than doubling the company's public float from 4.9% to 11.8% of shares outstanding, with the stock rising rather than falling on the news.

Svensk Maklarstatistik data released August 7 showed Swedish apartment (bostadsratter) prices fell 1.5% in July, the steepest monthly drop in a year, while detached house prices rose 0.9%, with the 12-month rate still positive at 4.6% for apartments and 3.4% for houses.

Czech residential building-plot prices reached CZK 2,615 per square meter in June 2026, up 7.3% year over year and 220% over the past decade, with listing-to-sale time nearly halving even as mortgage rates sit near 5.3%, according to a Hyponamiru.cz analysis published August 7.

Colliers data published August 3 showed CEE-6 commercial real estate investment volume rose to EUR 5.8 billion in H1 2026 from EUR 5.4 billion a year earlier, with Poland leading at over EUR 3 billion and the Czech Republic second at over EUR 1.4 billion, and residential/living allocation jumping to 19% of volume from 7%.

German commercial real estate lender Aareal Bank reported H1 2026 results on August 6 with adjusted operating profit of EUR 208 million, keeping it on track for its roughly EUR 400 million full-year target despite a pullback in its US lending book.

The US Treasury's OFAC sanctioned Dubai-based Shelbit Exchange, Iran-based Aban Tether, their founder Siavash Kayvanpour, and four affiliated front companies for laundering crypto proceeds to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps as part of a roughly $4 billion sanctions-evasion network.

Bybit filed a civil lawsuit against North Korea, its Reconnaissance General Bureau, and the Lazarus Group over the February 2025 hack that stole $1.5 billion, and secured a US court's preliminary injunction freezing identified stolen assets.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune filed a motion to proceed and cloture on the CLARITY Act, setting up a procedural vote shortly after the Senate returns from recess in mid-September, keeping the bill's 2026 prospects alive.

Cardano's ADA token completed the SEC's required six-month window of regulated CME futures trading, unlocking eligibility for the streamlined 75-day spot ETF review process and clearing a key hurdle for Grayscale's pending ADA ETF application.

US spot Ethereum ETFs pulled in roughly $245 million over the week ending August 7, their strongest weekly inflow in nearly four months, pushing cumulative net inflows to about $11.46 billion after a weak May and June.
China's central bank added about 20 tonnes of gold to its reserves in July 2026, its biggest monthly addition since October 2023, extending an official buying streak to 21 consecutive months.

The Trump administration announced roughly $3 billion in new US government financing for critical minerals and battery supply-chain projects, including Export-Import Bank loans for boron, graphite, tantalum and niobium, plus Pentagon-backed battery and scandium production.

Honeywell Aerospace, newly spun off from Honeywell, fell roughly 20-23% after its first standalone quarterly report missed estimates and it slashed 2026 organic sales growth guidance to 4-5% from 7-9% on supply-chain constraints favoring OEM deliveries over higher-margin aftermarket sales.

Axon Enterprise fell about 12-14% despite beating Q2 revenue and EPS estimates and raising full-year revenue growth guidance to 32-34%, as investors focused on software gross margin compression from 78.9% to 75.1% and rising component costs.

Trump renewed his effort to remove Fed Governor Lisa Cook over unproven mortgage-fraud allegations, giving her until August 26 to respond, reviving the Fed-independence legal battle after the Supreme Court's narrow 5-4 ruling left the door open for a second removal attempt.

The Fed held rates at 3.50%-3.75%, but markets now price a September hike as most likely and 9 of 18 FOMC members pencil in at least one 2026 hike under new Chair Kevin Warsh, a sharp widening of the hawkish dissent reported the prior week.

Ahead of the week's CPI and PPI prints, software prices rose 14% YoY and electronic-component wholesale prices rose 28% YoY, a new AI-capex-driven inflation channel the Fed is reportedly divided over as potentially structural rather than transitory.

The scale of the prior week's coordinated US-Japan yen intervention became clear: Japan spent an estimated $34 billion buying yen after it hit 40-year lows, and Bank of America now forecasts the yen strengthening about 6% to ¥149/dollar by year-end.

Barrick Mining reported Q2 2026 revenue of $3.68B (+16% YoY) and EPS of $0.47, with H1 free cash flow up 107% YoY to $770M funding $268M of Q2 buybacks plus a $0.15/share dividend, shares up ~5%, reinforcing the capital-returns case for gold miners amid record gold prices.

SpaceX's Q2 2026 earnings call disclosed Starlink has reached 12 million subscribers, doubling YoY, with management targeting $100B in annualized recurring revenue by year-end as the company is valued at $2.3 trillion post-IPO.

Prologis agreed to acquire UK logistics REIT Segro for roughly $18.8B, creating a combined $269B global logistics real estate platform and expanding Prologis' European footprint by 47%, with closing expected in H1 2027.

New Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac condo lending guidelines took effect requiring full HOA/condo association financial reviews instead of the prior limited-review shortcut, expected to slow approvals and disqualify more condo mortgage applicants.

CMBS office delinquency rates hit roughly 11.7%-12.3%, surpassing the 2008 financial-crisis peak by about 1.6 points, while the broader CMBS delinquency rate stood near 7.35% in June, reflecting continued distress concentrated in offices, lodging and retail.

Prague's office market remains structurally tight in 2026, with vacancy near 5.9% (lowest since early 2020), only about 30,400 sqm of new vacant supply expected this year, and prime inner-city rents up roughly 10% YoY, with most new projects not delivering until 2028.

UK annual house price growth slowed to 1.8% in July from 2.2% in June, and asking prices for new listings fell 1.0%, the largest July drop in a decade, as the average 2-year fixed mortgage rate jumped to 5.63% from 4.83% in February amid Iran-war-driven rate pressure.

The controversial BIP-110 Bitcoin soft-fork (a temporary ban on arbitrary data storage in transactions) triggered mandatory signaling at block 961,632 with under 1% miner support and split off into a breakaway chain that mined only two blocks before stalling, with roughly 99.85% of network hashpower staying on the main chain.

US spot Bitcoin ETFs closed the week ended Aug 7 with $853.54M in net inflows, their largest weekly total since mid-April, with BlackRock's IBIT alone taking in $693M across a six-day streak with zero outflow days.

A US court granted Bybit's request for a preliminary injunction freezing identified stolen assets tied to North Korea's Lazarus Group from the February 2025 $1.5B hack, moving the case from a filed lawsuit to an enforceable court order.

A Chinese court ruling confirmed Bitcoin and USDT hold legally protected property value under Chinese law even though the 2021 business trading ban remains in force, creating a legal contradiction that could affect asset-recovery and estate cases in China.

NY sugar futures hit a 10-month high and London white sugar an 11-month high as analysts swung 2026/27 global sugar forecasts from surplus to deficit on a weak India monsoon and an expected strong El Nino threatening Brazil, India and Thailand output.

Yemen's Houthis struck Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery (400,000 bpd) with a drone, sparking a fire, two days after Saudi Arabia signed a defense pact with Turkey and Pakistan; combined with stalled Hormuz reopening talks, oil extended gains a third session, Brent near $84 and WTI near $79, up over 5% in three days.

Indonesia's sovereign wealth fund Danantara took a 25% stake (potentially rising to 30%) in JBS's $8.1B Australasian meat operations, even as Fitch had already flagged Danantara's aggressive spending and governance concerns in a March 2026 negative outlook revision.

A report found PE-backed companies accounted for 50% of the largest ($1B+ liabilities) US corporate bankruptcies in H1 2026 despite PE representing only ~7% of the economy, while aging zombie funds unable to exit portfolio companies at claimed valuations were flagged as a growing systemic issue.

Valar Atomics raised a $1B Series B (at a $6B valuation) led by Sequoia to mass-produce modular nuclear reactors for AI data centers, while defense-tech firm Hadrian raised a $1.37B Series D (~$8B valuation), underscoring VC's pivot toward AI physical infrastructure.
